title: October 19, 1910: a boy was born in Lahore who would spend his career proving what crushes a dying star.
caption:
October 19, 1910: a boy was born in Lahore who would spend his career proving what crushes a dying star.

He moved to the US to pursue astrophysics, spending nearly six decades on the faculty at the University of Chicago until his death in 1995 - his uncle, C.V. Raman, had already won India's first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.

His theoretical work on how stars are structured and how they evolve, developed decades earlier, won him the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics, shared with William A. Fowler.

Chandrasekhar's Nobel came from pure astrophysical theory - proof that Indian scientific talent could reshape fundamental physics itself, not only build applied technology.
